what_would_change_verdict: A VIN decode confirming a 2001+ 3.0i (M54) would resolve the identity issue. A 2.8 would undercut the value case and the profile's engine minimum.
Trunk-floor and subframe photos or a PPI showing sound structure would move condition up. Any cracking or tearing would move it sharply down.
Dated cooling-system invoices would close the main model-critical gap.
Seller refusal of a VIN or PPI would move this down decisively.
evidence.mission_note: If the VIN confirms a 3.0i, this is a manual six-cylinder Z3 roadster at the bottom of the ideal budget band, exactly the enthusiast-bridge target. Accelerated-bridge mode still requires a remote PPI before money moves.
evidence.rationale: The listing establishes, through photos, a manual-transmission, apparently stock Z3 roadster in a deep metallic blue over tan, with clean paint, an uncracked dash, a tidy engine bay and fresh-looking Michelin run-flat tires. Its central problem is identity: it is listed as a 2000 'Z3 3.0i', a combination that did not exist in US model years, and there is no VIN to settle whether it is a MY2001 3.0i or a 2.8. The 'recent service' is an undated, unreceipted list of fluids, filters and tires that omits the cooling system entirely. Neither model-critical item, rear structure or cooling history, has any supporting evidence, and the car comes from coastal Florida. Title, owner and accident claims are seller statements only. At $10,000 it sits below the mileage-adjusted fair-value band, though that band assumes a 3.0i. The ad has been live since about January 2026 without a price change.
evidence.next_action: Message the seller for the VIN and a title photo, decode it to confirm model year and engine, and in the same message request trunk-floor and underside photos, cooling-system receipts and consent to a PPI at a Sarasota independent BMW shop.
